items.name: Plain Rice Manda
steps: Prepare 1450 ml (about 6 cups) hot water before starting Plain Rice Manda; keep one small ladle in reserve in case the base tightens early.
Boil the rice in abundant water until the grains open completely. Maintain moderate heat for 18–20 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.
Strain the thin starchy liquid without pressing the solids through. Let it drain for 1 minute without pressing harder than the recipe's texture requires.
Season the warm manda lightly and float the ghee on top. Leave the pan off the flame for 6 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Plain Rice Manda 5 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.

items.name: Cumin Rice Manda
steps: Bring 1450 ml (about 6 cups) water to a boil in a separate kettle and hold it hot, covered, so Cumin Rice Manda never loses its simmer.
Cook the rice in ample water until it releases its starch. Maintain medium-low heat for 18–20 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.
Pour the liquid through a fine strainer into a clean pot. Keep this stage to 7–9 minutes over gentle medium heat and stop when a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.
Stir in ground cumin, salt, and ghee while warm. Keep the pan over low heat for 2–3 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.
Rest Cumin Rice Manda 4 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.

items.name: Fennel Rice Manda
steps: Bring 1450 ml (about 6 cups) water to a boil in a separate kettle and hold it hot, covered, so Fennel Rice Manda never loses its simmer.
Simmer the rice slowly until the cooking water turns pearly. Maintain steady low heat for 19–21 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.
Strain off the fluid before the grains absorb it again. Let it drain for 1 minute without pressing harder than the recipe's texture requires.
Add ground fennel, a little salt, and melted ghee. Keep the pan over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.
Rest Fennel Rice Manda 7 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.

steps: Heat 1450 ml (about 6 cups) water until vigorously boiling, then lower it to a bare simmer beside the main pot for measured additions.

Boil the rice with grated ginger in a generous volume of water. Maintain gentle medium heat for 13–15 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.
Lift away the softened grains and retain the fragrant thin broth. Keep this stage to 8–10 minutes over low heat and stop when a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.
Season sparingly and add ghee immediately before serving. Leave the pan off the flame for 6 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.

Strain the liquid into a warmed serving pot. Let it drain for 2 minutes without pressing harder than the recipe's texture requires.
Whisk in coriander, salt, and a small spoon of ghee. Whisk for 50 seconds, scraping the bottom and corners until no dry pockets or lumps remain.
